title: High powers of a fibre-ample line bundle have locally liftable fibre sections
statement: Let $f:Z\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $S$ Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $s\in S$, and put $Z_s=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $L_s=L|_{Z_s}$, using module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $L_s$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There is an integer $d_0\geq0$ such that, for every integer $d\geq d_0$ and every $t\in\Gamma(Z_s,L_s^{\otimes d})$, there exist an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ and $\widetilde t\in\Gamma(f^{-1}(U),L^{\otimes d}|_{f^{-1}(U)})$ whose pullback to $Z_s$ is $t$. Tensor powers have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and the pullback uses the natural identification $(L^{\otimes d})|_{Z_s}\cong L_s^{\otimes d}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], iterated over the tensor factors.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, final assertion with F = O_Z: surjectivity of the degree-zero direct-image stalk to fibre sections, expressed by representatives of germs on open neighbourhoods.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_s$, and $k=A/\mathfrak m=\kappa(s)$. Choose a Noetherian affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the locally Noetherian cover containing $s$. The canonical-local-spectrum statement identifies $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ for the prime corresponding to $s$. Here is the elementary Noetherianity check: for any ideal $K\subset R_{\mathfrak p}$, its contraction to $R$ has finite generators $a_i$; every $a/u\in K$ has $a$ in that contraction, so the $a_i/1$ generate $K$. Thus $A$ is Noetherian, and in particular $\mathfrak m$ has finite generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$. The empty generating family is allowed when $A$ is a field.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof, specialized to F = O_Z

proof.text: Form $X=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$, with projections $h:X\to Z$ and $g:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and write $i:X_s=Z_s\hookrightarrow X$ for the closed fibre. Properness and closed immersions are preserved by base change. The single affine chart of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ makes it locally Noetherian, and the affine quasi-compactness theorem makes it Noetherian; likewise $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (a field has only two ideals). A proper map is of finite type, so finite-type preservation of Noetherianity shows that $Z$, $X$, and $X_s$ are Noetherian. Set $N=h^*L$ and $E_d=N^{\otimes d}$ for $d\ge0$. Pullback and tensor products preserve invertibility, so these are locally free of rank one, as are $L^{\otimes d}$ on $Z$. They are quasi-coherent of finite type by the definition of invertibility, and hence coherent by the locally Noetherian coherence criterion. Iterating pullback-tensor compatibility identifies $h^*(L^{\otimes d})=E_d$ and $i^*E_d=L_s^{\otimes d}$.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof, specialized to F = O_Z

proof.text: Let $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_X$, the ideal generated by the global functions $g^\sharp(a_j)$. Each $J^n$ is the image of a finite free module mapping to $\mathcal O_X$, using all degree-$n$ monomials in those functions; $J^0=\mathcal O_X$. Coherence of kernels and cokernels makes these images and $J^n/J^{n+1}$ coherent. Multiplication by $J$ kills $J^n/J^{n+1}$, so closed-immersion coherent equivalence regards it as a coherent module $G_n$ on $X_s$, with $i_*G_n=J^n/J^{n+1}$ and $G_0=\mathcal O_{X_s}$. Put $P=k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$, graded by total degree. Give $G=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}G_n$ the graded $g_s^*\widetilde P$-module structure in which $T_j$ acts by multiplication by $g^\sharp(a_j)$ modulo the next power of $J$. This is well defined: changing a representative in $J^n$ by $J^{n+1}$ changes its product by $J^{n+2}$; the coefficient action factors through $k$ because $\mathfrak m J^n\subset J^{n+1}$. Locally every element of $J^n$ is a sum of degree-$n$ monomials times local functions, and passage to its quotient has local lifts. Thus the one degree-zero section $1\in G_0$ generates $G$ over $g_s^*\widetilde P$. This verifies the finite-type graded-module hypothesis, including quasi-coherence of each piece, without an additional lemma.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof, specialized to F = O_Z

proof.text: Apply graded Serre vanishing on the proper $k$-scheme $g_s:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to the finite type graded $k$-algebra $P$, the finite type graded module $G$, and the ample invertible module $L_s$. It supplies one $d_0\ge0$ for which $H^1(X_s,G\otimes L_s^{\otimes d})=0$ for all $d\ge d_0$. Each $G_n$ is a retract of $G$: inclusion into the $n$th direct-sum component followed by projection is the identity. Tensoring and applying the cohomology functor preserve that identity. Hence $H^1(X_s,G_n\otimes L_s^{\otimes d})$ is a retract of zero and is zero, simultaneously for every $n\ge0$ and $d\ge d_0$. No exchange of an infinite sum and cohomology is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof, specialized to F = O_Z

proof.text: Fix $d\ge d_0$ and put $Q_n=E_d/J^nE_d$ for $n\ge1$. For each $n\ge1$ the quotient sequence has the short exact form $0\to (J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes E_d\to Q_{n+1}\to Q_n\to0$. Check this on an open trivializing the invertible $E_d$: it is $0\to J^n/J^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_X/J^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_X/J^n\to0$, and the identifications agree on overlaps. By the closed-immersion projection formula, its kernel is $i_*(G_n\otimes L_s^{\otimes d})$. The closed-immersion cohomology comparison and step 4 give zero $H^1$ of this kernel. The long exact cohomology sequence therefore makes $H^0(X,Q_{n+1})\to H^0(X,Q_n)$ surjective. Their composites $H^0(X,Q_k)\to H^0(X,Q_1)$ are surjective for every $k\ge1$ (identity for $k=1$, and induction by composition). All sheaves here are coherent: locally tensoring by $E_d$ is the identity, and the untwisted kernels and quotients are coherent by step 3.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof, specialized to F = O_Z

proof.text: Apply the cohomology-image stabilization theorem to the proper map $g$, the Noetherian ring $A$, the ideal $\mathfrak m$, the coherent module $E_d$, and degree $p=0$. Write $\rho_1:H^0(X,E_d)\to H^0(X,Q_1)$ for quotient restriction. Its assertion (2) gives a $c\ge0$ such that, for $k\ge1+c$, the image of $H^0(X,Q_k)\to H^0(X,Q_1)$ equals $\operatorname{Im}\rho_1$. The former image is all of $H^0(X,Q_1)$ by step 5. Thus $\rho_1$ is surjective. The auxiliary $c$ may depend on $d$; the bound $d_0$ was chosen in step 4 before $d$, so the required uniformity in $d$ is retained.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof, specialized to F = O_Z

proof.text: Apply the uncompleted local dictionary with $f:Z\to S$, $\mathcal F=L^{\otimes d}$ and $p=0$. Its stalk equivalence $a:(R^0f_*L^{\otimes d})_s\to H^0(X,E_d)$ and its finite-level comparison at index $0$ identify the map to $H^0(Z_s,L_s^{\otimes d})$ with $b_0\circ\rho_1\circ a$, where $b_0$ is an isomorphism. This map is surjective by step 6. Its value on the germ of a neighbourhood section is its pullback to $Z_s$, exactly the canonical-stalk-map property in the definition of formal fibre cohomology. In degree zero the derived functors are the ordinary sections and pushforward: in an injective resolution $0\to\mathcal F\to I^0\to I^1$, the degree-zero cycles after sections over any open are precisely the sections of $\mathcal F$, since sections preserve kernels. This also identifies their induced degree-zero maps with the ordinary section maps. Thus the surjection has domain $(f_*L^{\otimes d})_s$ and the asserted restriction formula on actual sections.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, proof, specialized to F = O_Z

proof.text: For the prescribed $t\in\Gamma(Z_s,L_s^{\otimes d})$, choose a preimage $z\in(f_*L^{\otimes d})_s$ under step 7. By the stalk description, $z$ is represented by a section on an open neighbourhood $U\ni s$. By the definition of module pushforward, this is a section $\widetilde t\in\Gamma(f^{-1}U,L^{\otimes d}|_{f^{-1}U})$. The canonical restriction formula of step 7 sends its germ to its pullback to $Z_s$, hence that pullback equals $t$. The neighbourhood can depend on $d$ and $t$, as allowed in the statement. If $Z_s$ is empty its section module is zero and the zero section already provides the conclusion.

Statement: it matches the final assertion of Stacks 0D2M (coherent.tex l.5973) with F=O_X: f proper, S Noetherian, L_s ample, and d_0 chosen before d and t. Stalk surjectivity is written as an open U, a section t~ on f^{-1}U and its pullback. Nothing is weakened, and this is exactly the form the parent 0D2N node uses. Steps: (1) A=R_p is Noetherian (elementary). (2) Base change keeps properness, X, Z and X_s are Noetherian, and E_d is invertible, hence coherent. (3) J^n is coherent, G_n comes from the 087T node, and G is a finite-type graded k[T]-module generated by 1, with the local generation argument checked. (4) The 0897(2) node applies with A=k, P finitely generated, g_s proper and L_s ample; the bound is uniform in n through the retract argument. (5) The quotient sequences, the closed-immersion projection formula and the cohomology node give H^0(Q_k)->H^0(Q_1) surjective. (6) The node's assertion (2) is source 02OB(3) (l.5553), the same use as the source; it gives rho_1 surjective, and c depends only on d after d_0 is fixed. (7) The local dictionary at n=0 gives kappa_0=b_0 rho_1 a, so kappa_0 is surjective, and IsFormalFunctionsTheta gives the pullback formula, with no flat base change used. (8) Germ representatives. Edge cases checked: field base (r=0), Artinian base, empty fibre, non-flat f. Duplicates: rg for 0D2M and ample-on-fibre finds only the item and its parent; there are no new nodes and no SGA. Tool_uses accepted: these are generic Noetherian cohomology tools that the unit sk-i-curve-zero does not provide; the declared definitions are harmless. No fixes.
